newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq ends lower, snapping four-session advance.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq ends lower, snapping four-session advance.

text.p: A late-session slump by high-technology stocks sent Nasdaq shares to a lower close, snapping a four-session advance in the tech-dominated market.
Traders said stocks were hit by a wave of late-day profit taking after an earlier upturn in Treasuries lost steam. The 30-year bond was off 1/32 to yield 7.10 in late trading.
"After midday they just fizzled and faded," said Brian Finnerty, senior vice president at Unterberg Harris, of Nasdaq stocks.

The Nasdaq composite finished off about eight points, or 0.6 percent, at 1249. The composite index had risen about 56 points in the previous three trading days, rebounding from a sharp selloff that clipped 13.5 percent off the index from its January 22 record closing level.
Among large-cap tech shares, Intel Corp fell 4-23/64 to 142-1/4, Microsoft Corp dropped 1/4 to 98 and Cisco Systems Inc fell 1-5/16 to 54-1/16.
Micron Electronics Inc rose 1-1/8 to 23-1/2 after PC Week Online reported the Idaho-based mail-order computer company had been approached about a possible merger.
